body:
Chairman and CEO at Microsoft

We're redefining the SDLC for the agentic era. Lots of GitHub updates this morning at Universe: • GitHub Copilot Fusion delivers frontier-level quality, 40% faster and at up to 77% lower cost • Our unified Copilot harness is now in Foundry, a managed service for building long-running agents that reason, use tools, and get work done • Copilot Projects gives you an orchestration loop to build with multiple agents across repos And we’re expanding capacity and strengthening GitHub’s architecture to make the home of agentic development more resilient. Read more: https://lnkd.in/gvtEeair

Satya Nadella This does not match with what your company is trying to do. 60000 voluntry exit suggests that you are out of ideas. Copilot is a waste of energy. It's the most hated model on this planet. Microsoft windows is a decaying OS. your company is not helping a bit on UX. Every click is taking longer and longer as the machine goes old. Sharepoint makes copies of the same document. redundant copies. OneDrive does too. Your servers are getting heavy by each edit. incrementally. Every Office app has 1000 of buttons. It's like operating a cockpit. Instead of giving voluntary exit to those poor employees maybe you should think about these UX bugs. Otherwise, a new OS will steamroll your business.

Dario D. what happens to the people whose knowledge and labor built the entire system? Their years of commits and PR reviews quietly become the training data for the agents replacing them :)

The line I'd underline in the announcement has no feature attached: "Developers set the direction, make decisions, and stay accountable for what ships." Once agents run in parallel across repos, the pace of shipping is set by the pace of deciding, and that part doesn't scale with compute. It rarely sits inside engineering either: someone on the business side still has to say yes. The SDLC is no longer linear. The approval chain around it still is.

Well, claiming that 99%of all software in history will be written within the next five years mixes sheer volume with genuine utility. Generating endless lines of boilerplate does not equate to solving structural problems. Most software engineering organisations spend their time trying to remove obsolete code rather than inflating their codebases. The shift towards consumption billing explains much of Microsoft enthusiasm here. GitHub Enterprise customers no longer need a separate seat subscription, yet they must purchase AI credits to fund these autonomous loops. When autonomous agents run parallel sessions across different repositories, drafting issues & reviewing their own output, the credit counter ticks constantly. That financial model rewards sheer activity over precision. A customer pays for every failed test run, every circular revision, and every speculative merge request initiated by an agent. There is also an obvious circularity in building automated review systems to evaluate automated pull requests. When developers must spend their days supervising a torrent of machine produced changes, the burden of verification increases rather than disappears, this is huge cost to customers. Thx

Satya Nadella As software development evolves from AI-assisted coding to multi-agent orchestration, productivity is only part of the equation. The harder challenge is ensuring that each agent operates within its authorized scope, that changes are independently validated, and that the final software meets its intended requirements. As execution becomes more autonomous, verification and accountability must evolve alongside it. The future of SDLC is not just about producing software faster, but ensuring that what gets delivered is what was intended—and can be verified.

Love it. We’re really getting closer to a world where developers spend more time reviewing, directing, and validating code than writing every line themselves. One thing we’d pay particular attention to though is how permissions work across repositories. Giving agents the ability to read, modify, and execute code across multiple projects raises some interesting security questions.

Satya Nadella 1/2 Satya, GitHub Universe 2026 is redefining the Software Development Lifecycle. But Microsoft's workforce decisions raise a much bigger question: what exactly are we optimizing? 2025: approximately 15,000 jobs eliminated. July 2026: another 4,800 positions eliminated. October 26: voluntary exit offers extended to approximately 60,000 employees, eligibility, not actual departures. FY2026: $115.9 billion invested in property and equipment, alongside $133.7 billion in net income. And today: 40% faster, up to 77% lower cost. These figures do not prove that AI caused the workforce reductions. But they demand a broader definition of progress. 77% lower cost for whom? For the agent? The enterprise? The shareholder? The customer? And what happens to the people whose knowledge and labor built the entire system?

curious how copilot projects handles two agents changing the same dependency

A race car without good brakes is just a faster way to crash. AI can write code faster, but speed becomes dangerous when people mistake getting things done for getting things right.
